## Overview

In BaZi, the Day Master is the stem of your day pillar — the "you" at the centre of the chart. Yours is Gui 癸 (Yin Water), a soft, receptive, mist-and-dew kind of water, born in the Xin Mao 辛卯 month pillar. That month's stem is Xin 辛 (Yin Metal), an Indirect Resource star (learning, intuition and support that arrives sideways rather than by the obvious route), and its branch Mao 卯 (Rabbit) carries Yi 乙 (Yin Wood) as main qi, an Eating God star (creativity, enjoyment and the impulse to make and share). Metal in that month generates Water, so the season itself feeds your Day Master.

That is why your chart reads as a strong Day Master. Supporting elements — the Friend, Rob Wealth and Resource stars that strengthen Gui — make up 67.1% of the balance, with Metal the strongest element at 40% (count 3) and Water second at 27.1% (count 2). A strong Gui has plenty of depth and stamina but can become over-full, so the chart is eased by the elements that give Water somewhere to go: Fire at 7.1% (the weakest element, scarce but present), Earth at 8.2% and Wood at 17.6%. Fire, Earth and Wood are your favorable elements; Water and Metal are unfavorable.

The central theme is a resource-rich, reflective personality that benefits from being drawn outward into expression, usefulness and warmth. The Nobleman (Tian Yi Gui Ren) star touches both your year pillar and month pillar through its branches Mao and Si, which adds a helpful-people thread to family and working life, while the Void (Kong Wang) touching your day pillar suggests you sometimes feel a little detached from your own centre and do best with grounded routines.

## Personality

Two Xin 辛 (Yin Metal) Indirect Resource stems sit in your year and month pillars, and the day branch You 酉 (Rooster) also hides Xin as its main qi, again Indirect Resource. Resource of the indirect kind is the mind that learns by absorption and intuition rather than by syllabus: you notice patterns, read atmospheres and often understand something before you can explain it. With Metal at 40%, this is the loudest voice in the chart — a careful, precise, sometimes perfectionist inner critic that wants things to be right before they are shown.

Balancing that is your Eating God in the month branch, Yi 乙 (Yin Wood) as main qi — the part of you that enjoys craft, humour, good food and the pleasure of making something for its own sake. When this side is allowed out, the Metal softens and your natural charm comes through. Your hour pillar, Gui Chou 癸丑, adds a Friend stem (peers, equals, the urge to belong) over a Chou 丑 (Ox) branch whose main qi Ji 己 (Yin Earth) is a Seven Killings star — pressure, challenge and the drive it creates. That combination describes someone who is sociable but quietly self-demanding.

A habit worth adjusting: because Resource is so heavy, you may over-prepare, over-research and delay the moment of doing. The Void touching your day pillar can add a sense of "is this really me?" when you are under strain. Naming your own preferences out loud, even small ones, keeps the strong Water from pooling into passivity.

## Career

Your working environment is read from the month pillar, Xin Mao 辛卯 — Indirect Resource over Eating God. This is a thoughtful, idea-led professional style: research, writing, design, analysis, teaching or any role where insight is turned into something others can use. Because Eating God is favorable, work that lets you produce, present or perform suits you far better than work that only requires you to absorb. The Scholar (Wen Chang) star touches your month pillar through its branch Mao, reinforcing a natural fit with study, credentials and knowledge-based work.

The Direct Officer star appears twice in useful places: as the residual qi Wu 戊 (Yang Earth) in your year branch Si 巳 (Snake) and, more prominently, as the stem of your current Wu Zi 戊子 Luck Pillar, which is favorable. Direct Officer is the star of responsibility, structure and legitimate authority — the satisfaction of a clearly defined role done well. In this decade, taking on titled responsibility, managing a process or earning a formal qualification tends to sit well with you.

Where to be careful: the Seven Killings in your hour pillar's main qi means you can push yourself under pressure and take on challenges that look like proving something rather than building something. Choose the demanding role that also teaches you a skill, and let the Nobleman star do its work — ask for introductions and mentorship rather than assuming you must arrive self-made.

## Wealth

Wealth in BaZi is not a prediction of amounts; it describes the shape of your relationship with money. Your wealth stars are Fire, and Fire is your weakest element at 7.1% — scarce but present, and favorable. Direct Wealth appears as the main qi Bing 丙 (Yang Fire) in your year branch Si, tying early-family and background matters to steady, earned income. Indirect Wealth appears as the main qi Ding 丁 (Yin Fire) in the 2026 annual branch, and it is the stem Ten God of your next Luck Pillar, Ding Hai 丁亥.

With wealth stars scarce, money tends to arrive through deliberate effort and structured choices rather than windfalls or flair. Your strong Resource side is an asset here: you are good at learning the rules of a system before acting inside it. The risk is over-caution — waiting for perfect information while an opportunity passes. The Eating God in your month branch suggests that income may flow most naturally from what you genuinely enjoy creating, so putting time into a craft or skill you like is a sound money habit, not a distraction.

Practical shape: keep spending tied to visible plans, review your budget on a regular rhythm rather than in anxious bursts, and treat raises or role changes (the Direct Officer theme of this decade) as the main route to growth rather than side ventures you have not researched. A short written review each season suits your Metal-heavy, detail-loving mind.

## Love and Relationships

Close relationships are read from the day branch, and yours is You 酉 (Rooster), whose main qi Xin 辛 (Yin Metal) is Indirect Resource. This suggests you show affection through attentiveness — remembering details, thinking about your partner's needs, solving problems quietly. It also means you can retreat into your own head when hurt, processing inwardly instead of saying the thing out loud. The Void touching your day pillar can make you question whether you are truly known, even when you are.

The Direct Wealth star in your year branch (Bing as main qi in Si) is the traditional partner star for a male chart, and it sits in the year pillar — family background and long-standing ties matter to you, and a relationship may grow from a context you already belong to rather than a wholly new scene. The Nobleman (Tian Yi Gui Ren) touching your year and month pillars is a warm signature: people tend to want to help you, and introductions through friends and family are a natural way to meet someone.

Your hour pillar's Friend stem Gui 癸 over a Seven Killings main qi in Chou describes the push-pull of closeness: you want companionship and equality (Friend), but you also test yourself and others under pressure (Seven Killings). The habit to adjust is letting small frictions become internal audits. Say what you need in plain words early, and let the Eating God's playfulness into the relationship — shared food, jokes and creative projects do more for your bond than perfect understanding.

## Wellbeing Habits

Your chart is Metal-dominant at 40% and Water-strong at 27.1%, with Fire the weakest element at 7.1%. In everyday terms this reads as a constitution that runs cool, dry and mentally busy — so the habits that serve you are warming, grounding and loosening rather than more stimulation. Sleep is the first lever: with heavy Resource energy, your mind keeps processing after the day ends, so a wind-down that starts well before bed (dim light, no new information, something warm to drink) suits you better than pushing through.

Food: with Fire scarce, favour warm, cooked, gently spiced meals over cold and raw ones, and eat at regular times — the Eating God in your month branch is literally the star of appetite and enjoyment, so meals you actually look forward to are part of the practice, not an indulgence. Movement: Earth is your second-favorable element at 8.2% and the Ox in your hour pillar carries the Goat Blade (Yang Ren) star, found from your day stem and touching that hour pillar — a signature of physical vigour that wants an outlet. Steady, rhythmic exercise (walking, hiking, weights, martial practice) suits you better than erratic bursts.

Emotionally, the Seven Killings in your hour pillar's main qi describes internal pressure that builds quietly. A short daily check-in — naming one thing that went well and one thing that is still nagging — keeps that pressure from becoming background noise, and time outdoors in sunlight gives your scarce Fire some room. If you feel unwell, please consult a qualified healthcare professional.

## Current Luck Pillar

A Luck Pillar is a ten-year layer of influence, set by a stem and branch that colour the tone of that decade the way weather colours a season. Your current one is Wu Zi 戊子 (2023–2032, East Asian ages 23–32). Its stem Wu 戊 (Yang Earth) is a Direct Officer star — responsibility, structure and legitimate authority — and it is favorable. Its branch Zi 子 (Rat) carries Gui 癸 (Yin Water) as main qi, a Friend star (peers, equals and the pull of the group), and that is unfavorable for a strong Day Master.

Read together, these ten years have a clear shape: the outward structure is good for you, while the inward pull toward sameness is the thing to manage. A titled role, a formal commitment or a demanding but clearly defined path tends to bring out your best, because Earth gives your strong Water a bank to flow within. Meanwhile the Friend star in the branch can scatter focus — too many peers, too many group opinions, too much comfort in the familiar. The favourable side of this decade is the one that asks you to take a defined position; the unfavourable side is the one that keeps you in the crowd.

Your next Luck Pillar, Ding Hai 丁亥 (2033–2042, East Asian ages 33–42), shifts the emphasis noticeably. Its stem Ding 丁 (Yin Fire) is an Indirect Wealth star — resourcefulness, opportunities that arrive through your own initiative — and it is favorable, so the theme moves from duty and structure toward enterprise and adaptable income. Its branch Hai 亥 (Pig) carries Ren 壬 (Yang Water) as main qi, a Rob Wealth star (competition, strong peers, the urge to go your own way), which is unfavorable. The decade ahead asks you to build on the structure of the current one while becoming more entrepreneurial and more comfortable with rivalry.

## Year by Year

Each Chinese solar year begins at Li Chun, the start of spring, so the annual pillar roughly matches the calendar year but starts a little before it. The readings below follow the years in order, with the annual stem and branch, the Luck Pillar in force, and any relations to your natal chart.

### 2026 丙午 · Bing Wu

The year stem Bing 丙 (Yang Fire) is a Direct Wealth star (steady, earned income and reliable resources), and Fire is favorable; the year branch Wu 午 (Horse) also carries favorable Fire, with Ding 丁 (Yin Fire) as main qi — an Indirect Wealth star — and Ji 己 (Yin Earth) as middle qi, a Seven Killings star. You are still inside your Wu Zi 戊子 Luck Pillar. The overall tone is a year in which practical money matters and visible results come into focus, supported by the decade's Direct Officer structure. It is a good time to put effort into a defined project where the return is tangible.

Two stem combinations link this year to your roots: the year stem Bing combines with the Xin in your year pillar and with the Xin in your month pillar. In plain terms, the wealth theme of the year meets your Resource nature — your instinct to learn and prepare — and may either sharpen your commercial judgement or tempt you to over-think the terms. The year branch Wu clashes with the Zi branch of your Wu Zi Luck Pillar, so the steady background of this decade may feel more changeable this year; keep plans flexible and revisit them in the second half rather than locking everything early in the year.

### 2027 丁未 · Ding Wei

The year stem Ding 丁 (Yin Fire) is an Indirect Wealth star (resourcefulness and opportunities you create for yourself), and Fire is favorable; the year branch Wei 未 (Goat) is favorable Earth, with Ji 己 (Yin Earth) as main qi — a Seven Killings star — Ding 丁 as middle qi (Indirect Wealth) and Yi 乙 (Yin Wood) as residual qi (Eating God). Still in your Wu Zi 戊子 Luck Pillar, this year leans toward initiative and self-generated opportunity, with a challenge element (Seven Killings) that keeps you on your toes.

The relations are mixed and worth naming plainly. The year branch Wei forms a three-harmony link with your month pillar branch Mao, which supports the working-environment side of your chart and may bring cooperation or a productive new connection. At the same time, Wei clashes with your hour pillar branch Chou and forms a punishment with it, so the hour-pillar themes — friends, peers, and your own drive under pressure — may feel more stirred up. Keep group dynamics light, avoid turning a small disagreement into a principle, and give yourself room to rest when the pressure rises.

### 2028 戊申 · Wu Shen

The year stem Wu 戊 (Yang Earth) is a Direct Officer star, and Earth is favorable; the year branch Shen 申 (Monkey) is unfavorable Metal, with Geng 庚 (Yang Metal) as main qi — a Direct Resource star (learning, support and steady backing) — Ren 壬 (Yang Water) as middle qi (Rob Wealth: competition and strong peers) and Wu 戊 as residual qi (Direct Officer). Still in your Wu Zi Luck Pillar, the tone is structural and career-facing on the surface, with a heavy Metal undertow that can over-feed your already strong Resource side.

The relations are busy. The year stem Wu combines with both the Gui in your day pillar and the Gui in your hour pillar — the Direct Officer theme meeting your own Day Master and your Friend star — which can feel like responsibility stepping right up to your sense of self and your social circle. The year branch Shen forms a six harmony with your year pillar branch Si, supportive for background and family matters, yet also a punishment with the same Si, so those matters may carry a mix of ease and friction. Shen also forms a three-harmony link with the Zi of your Luck Pillar and clashes nothing else — a year to lean into structured learning and formal support, while watching the urge to compete for its own sake.

### 2029 己酉 · Ji You

The year stem Ji 己 (Yin Earth) is a Seven Killings star, and Earth is favorable; the year branch You 酉 (Rooster) is unfavorable Metal, with Xin 辛 (Yin Metal) as main qi — an Indirect Resource star. Still in your Wu Zi Luck Pillar. The tone is a year of challenge and self-testing (Seven Killings), backed by a great deal of reflective, inward Metal energy — good for deep work and study, less good for quick decisions or crowded rooms.

The relations cluster tightly around your chart. The year branch You forms a three-harmony link with your year pillar branch Si and another with your hour pillar branch Chou, which can bring support from background and from your peer circle at the same time. But You clashes with your month pillar branch Mao — the working-environment branch — so routines and day-to-day work rhythms may feel more changeable, and You forms a punishment with your day pillar branch You, your own day branch. With your sense of self stirred this way, slow down, talk things through, and give the perfectionist in you something concrete to finish rather than something abstract to worry over.

### 2030 庚戌 · Geng Xu

The year stem Geng 庚 (Yang Metal) is a Direct Resource star, and Metal is unfavorable; the year branch Xu 戌 (Dog) is favorable Earth, with Wu 戊 (Yang Earth) as main qi — a Direct Officer star — Xin 辛 as middle qi (Indirect Resource) and Ding 丁 as residual qi (Indirect Wealth). You are still in your Wu Zi 戊子 Luck Pillar this year. The tone is a pull in two directions: the stem over-supplies your strong Resource side, while the branch's Earth supports the decade's constructive Officer theme. Lean into practical, role-based work and let learning serve a task rather than become the task.

The relations are gentler than in recent years. The year branch Xu forms a six harmony with your month pillar branch Mao, which is a supportive pairing for your working environment — a good time to build relationships with colleagues or make a work arrangement more comfortable. Xu also forms a punishment with your hour pillar branch Chou, so the pressure-and-peers theme of the hour pillar may still niggle. Pay attention to that in the first half of the year, and let the second half settle into the more cooperative rhythm.

## Guidance

- Put regular time into warmth and expression — a creative hobby, cooking, music or presenting your work — because Fire is your scarcest element at 7.1% and it is favorable.
- Choose at least one clearly defined responsibility this decade, such as a titled role or a formal qualification, because the Direct Officer stem of your Wu Zi 戊子 Luck Pillar is favorable and suits you.
- Guard against over-preparation: set a small deadline each season for showing something unfinished, since Indirect Resource dominates your Metal-heavy chart and tends to delay the moment of doing.
- Keep a short, regular money review rather than waiting for a big decision moment, because your wealth stars are scarce Fire and benefit from steady, deliberate attention.
- Seek out the people your Nobleman (Tian Yi Gui Ren) star points to — mentors and helpful introductions through family and work — since that star touches both your year pillar and month pillar.
